quest.title: Fairground Gathering, Summer Lights Illuminated
quest.description: The third component of the Central Hub fell in the forest to the north. Idyia mentioned that the cousin Eula was searching for has gone to this area as well. Perhaps you'll be able to find something that hints at his whereabouts...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Collei and Eula. Oh, Idyia is here, too!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #Hey, it's {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: How are you? Did you rest well?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm feeling refreshed!

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Yep, this is a comfortable place to rest, I guess that's one thing here that's better than the desert... But other than that, there's not much going for this place.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Saying things like that isn't going to help, Idyia!

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: But it's the truth. The desert is full of terrible memories for me, being there was like... yeah, like wading through thick mud.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a weird way to put it... Actually, if you hadn't mentioned it, Paimon would have already forgotten that this domain is in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I know what you mean, the air here isn't at all like the desert. It's very humid, almost as if we're in the rainforest. It's a very familiar feeling for me.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Everyone looks well-rested. If you're ready, we can start making our way to the jungle north of here.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Good luck, everyone! I'll be rooting for you!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Hold on, I said "we," didn't I? No need to say goodbye, because you're coming too.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Huh? But wait, I'm just the Mascot!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You can't back out this time, Idyia! The manager of the fairgrounds is waiting to see you. She said, "Idyia is the only person who could help."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "The Fairgrounds"?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Yes, Collei and I discovered a fairgrounds in the forest.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: The person in charge of it seems to be a Spantamad scholar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A scholar? But what's she doing there, researching the forest's Ley Lines?

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wish there were Ley Lines here that I could have her study... Anyway, I know who you're talking about. I'd better come along then.

talks.objective: Go to the forest in the north
Keep heading towards the forest in the north
Keep heading towards the forest in the north

dialogues.text: Ah, finally! Someone has arrived...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Sorry to keep you waiting, Maymunah. We've brought Idyia with us.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Thank you, Collei. It's been quite some time since I've seen you, Idyia. To be honest, I didn't think you'd actually show up...

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: If anything, I thought you'd be curled up somewhere crying alone.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Hey, you shouldn't be saying things like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, doesn't seem to be the first time Paimon's heard someone say that about Idyia though...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: You want to see me cry? Fine! I'll start crying right here!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah! No, please don't!

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, I shouldn't have said that. Now, who are these two?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Hi, I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Paimon is Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: They're reliable helpers, lucky for you that I found them. You'd better be more careful about how you speak to them, okay!?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Of course. Good to meet you, you may call me Maymunah. For the sake of time, we should forego the usual pleasantries. Please, follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wow...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look at that huge tent...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Amazing, isn't it? I helped make it. What fun would a fairground be without a tent, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Paimon knew you couldn't be so pathetic! You just act modest all the time to hide your actual abilities!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: What is it, Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Uh, sorry... I'm not sure if I should tell you...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm afraid it might dampen the mood...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: That's not important, please just speak your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Uh, well... There are lots of vendor booths set up here, but there's no one running them. In fact, there's no one at this fair at all. It looks pretty deserted...

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: *sigh* The truth is, this used to be an exciting and bustling place.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: But just a few days ago, something happened and it seemed like...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like "the world was suddenly flipped upside down"?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Yes, exactly! Something fell from the Central Hub into the tent, and knocked down the Crystal Light that was hanging at the top.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Ah, the Crystal Light...

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. I remember a certain someone said that we should have beautiful lights to celebrate at a fair, and made us that Crystal Light.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: But once the light fell, the tent became a complete mess and the Hydro Eidolons were trapped inside.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Just when I was at my wits' end, a man from the Lawrence Clan came and offered his assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Wait, he offered to help you?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Yes, and he refused to listen to any of my warnings. He just walked straight into the tent, and then...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Yes? And then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, don't leave us hanging here! What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: And that's it... He became trapped inside along with the Hydro Eidolons.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yet another victim...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh no, we have to do something. We can't just leave him there, Maymunah!

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: I know, but the situation inside might be more difficult than you think. You should mentally prepare yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Just talking about it is a waste of time. Since we're already here, let's go and scout out the situation ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright. This way, please.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: There used to be a large stage inside, but after everything got shaken up, it seems the very nature of the entire place was altered.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: The lamps and Crystal Light that were hanging above have all fallen down, which makes repairs near impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wait, so you mean it's difficult to move around in there?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Yes, mainly because of the lights.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Do any of you have experience being on stage? Once the stage lights turn on, everyone's attention is focused on you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I can't stand that feeling. Having everyone's attention focused solely on me would just make me feel terrible.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Me too! I'm no good at speaking in front of people, and then to have everyone staring at you... Ugh, just the thought of it makes me shudder.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Sounds like you have some things you haven't been able to let go of yet.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: *sigh* Please don't laugh. I'm trying my best to change that, but there are still some things I can't overcome. Like when there's a lot of people around, or when people are staring at me...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: No, there's nothing funny about that... and you know what? It's not a bad thing to care when other people are looking.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: That's my opinion, anyway. Think about it, only people who have high standards for themselves would worry about failing to meet others' expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: You have many good qualities, Collei. I bet if you had to learn dance since childhood like myself, then you'd be an even better dancer than me.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No, no way! That would be impossible!

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: (I can relate. I know exactly how she feels.)

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Maybe we should find a time for you to learn with me, and one day you will become an outstanding dancer, too. By that time, you'll be so focused on performing your beautiful moves that you'll no longer worry about an audience watching you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Eula's so passionate about this that she's practically glowing now.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Really, you'd do that? You wouldn't think I look stupid and secretly laugh at me, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Hmph, you really think I'm that kind of person? Fine, vengeance will be mine.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, no! Of course not! Alright, please teach me.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Seems there's no need for me to warn you again. Anyway, you just need to open the curtain and you'll be able to see the stage.

talks.objective: Unlock and raise the Crystal Light
Head to the second floor of the large tent

dialogues.text: Hello? Is anyone here? If you can hear me, please help!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Lessig Lawrence?

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Wh—Who are you? Who has the audacity to utter my full name?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, you sure don't look like you're in any condition to be talking like that.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Yep, he's a member of the Lawrence Clan all right. Even though he's hanging on by thread, he still insists on clinging to meaningless etiquette.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: You... What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Hah! Have you come here to mock me, Eula?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: If you would just think for a moment, it should be pretty obvious why we are here. Yet now you're intentionally trying to provoke me?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Of course, you don't have to accept my help. After all, "Aristocrats are naturally superior and need no help from others."

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: ...Yes, thanks for the reminder, I don't need help from the likes of you!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I don't think he really means it, Eula.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: His tone was harsh, but he keeps glancing at you from the corner of his eyes. It's my opinion as the Healer that he needs help.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Hmph. He's been trapped for so long that it seems he's forgotten how to hold a decent conversation. How ridiculous. Let's go. We'll leave the stage to this person who'd rather save face than save his own life.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Hey, n—no... Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Halt! You cannot just leave me here! W—We're both of the Lawrence bloodline, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Helping me when necessary certainly won't tarnish your prestige! If anything, my embarrassing predicament will be overshadowed by your virtuous deed. W—We must uphold the prestige and dignity of the family!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: This is the best reason you could come up with? You think tacking on the word "family" will be enough to talk me into helping you?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: You should be ashamed for your careless actions. It's because of you that we all had to come here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems everyone in the Lawrence Clan is this way. They'll do anything to save face...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Alright, alright, looks like it's time for the Mascot to step in.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Here you go. One for Eula and one for Lessig.

response.speaker: Lessig
response.text: What is this? Candy?

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Uh, thanks.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh! This smell! It's just like the aroma I smelled coming from the lens.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Yes, that's right. Enjoying something sweet always lightens the mood.

response.speaker: Lessig
response.text: Thank you, Miss Mascot. I certainly do feel much better now.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: (Hmph, so he's willing to thank someone else, but not me?)

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Eula has been worrying about you the past few days, and asked me several times regarding how to find you.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: But now that you two have been reunited, I won't have to keep answering her questions anymore. Ah, I'm so happy!

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Let me clarify one thing, I don't care what happens to him! If you're going to keep saying nonsense like this, then...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Eula will never admit that she actually cares about him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're probably right.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: If you're going to keep saying nonsense like this, then... then at least give me another piece of candy.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Hmm? Oh, sure, sure! I still have more!

response.speaker: Lessig
response.text: ...Sorry, I admit my mistake. I know I've caused heaps of trouble for all of you.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Hmph, why couldn't you have just said that earlier?

response.speaker: Maymunah
response.text: I'm back... Oh? Have you already finished catching up? Why are you all looking at me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh... nothing. Don't mind us.

response.speaker: Maymunah
response.text: Alright, then let's clean things up here and keep working our way toward getting the Crystal Light fixed! Ah, there's no need to push yourself in your condition, Lessig.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I'll take him and find someplace for him to rest. I happen to be a little tired myself.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Alright. I'll leave my cousin to you, then.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: You'd better rest up and regain your strength before we settle things, Lessig.

choices.text: We did come all the way here to save him...

talks.objective: Unlock and raise the Crystal Light
Head to the third floor of the large tent

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, another path has appeared! This should be the last level.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Yes, don't worry. We're almost to the top of the tent.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: The last thing we need to do is raise the Crystal Light to the very top of the tent.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: After the stage collapsed, I realized that having it raised only half-way makes it look a lot like the stage at the Grand Bazaar. Have any of you visited the Grand Bazaar before?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: No, I haven't.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I have. I've gone there a few times with Master Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: The place is bustling with all kinds of vendors! And if you're lucky, you can see Nilou perform her dance.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Oh, a dance from Sumeru? I'd like to see that myself. Hmm, if only it were on the way back, then we could stop there.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It doesn't matter if it's on the way or not. I would be happy to take you whenever you have time, Eula!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Great, I'll take you up on that offer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've been to the Grand Bazaar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, now that Paimon thinks about it, we've already been there more times than Paimon can remember!

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Really? My father used to help with festivities at the Grand Bazaar and would always give me candy during the events.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: I was just a kid and didn't understand anything... I was happy as long as he gave me some candy. To me, fairs and festivals were the best things ever.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: I always thought my father was amazing, and wanted to be just like him when I grew up.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But aren't you a scholar in the Akademiya, Maymunah? As far as I know, scholars seldom can spend time doing anything but research.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I doubt you could have time to assist your father in preparing festivities.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Yeah, seems you read me like a book.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: When I had the choice between becoming who I wanted to be and who my parents wanted me to be, I ended up choosing the latter... But I was never happy about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that's almost the exact opposite of Eula's situation.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: You must have already realized that. Why else would you set up all the booths here and make this place like a fairgrounds?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Yes, but... I'm still not as happy as I imagined I would be.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: I realized that attending a fair and running a fair are two completely different things.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: The main reason my childhood was so fun and carefree is because my family worked hard.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: But my father knew how difficult and tiring running a fair could be, so he wanted to push me towards academics.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: *sigh* But in the end, I didn't do well in either.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: I gave up on myself and resorted to investigating Ley Lines in the desert. Some things happened and then I accidentally ended up here.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: I finally had a chance to make my wish of running a fair come true, but after seeing everything come crashing down, I feel like I've lost the strength to go on.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It's not as bad as you make it out to be, Maymunah. No need to feel so down.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You have the courage to change, and you've been actively guiding us on this journey.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Someone who's given up on themself could never do these things.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Collei...

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: I understand my situation better than anyone, you don't need to try to comfort me.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It's not that I'm trying to comfort you, it's just that people sometimes don't realize that their own actions speak louder than words.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Believe me, this is something that I learned from my time together with Eula.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Oh? What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, uh nothing! Ahem, now let's get that Crystal Light fixed.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: ...Alright.

talks.objective: Light the lanterns at the Fairgrounds
Light the lanterns at the Fairgrounds

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Idyia, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Oh! I was starting to wonder what was taking you so long! But don't worry, Lessig is recovering well.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Hehe, I'm pretty good at taking care of people. Seems I've found another good thing about myself...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I don't know if I should be worried for him or happy for her...

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: The shadow... it's massive!!! Ah, wait! The shadow just now, it's... Ah!

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Uh, ahem... Seems he still might need a little more time to recover. Tell me, did everything go well for you all?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: #Of course. With a team like {NICKNAME}, Paimon, Collei and Eula, they're at least 40 times more reliable than you ever were.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Only 40 times more reliable? That means I'm still pretty good, then.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Ugh... I guess it's impossible to feel like you've lost once you've already given up... I'm a little concerned about how comfortable you are with that...

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Huh!? What has happened? How did I get outside of the tent!?

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Ah, that's right... I remember meeting Eula, and then... and then, ugh... my head...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Ah, you're awake now. Don't worry, that's just a side effect of your treatment, Lessig.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I still feel a little disoriented...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm scared to ask what kind of treatment he's receiving...)

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Lessig Lawrence.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you, Eula! Alright, alright, I'll do it... I'll come back to Mondstadt with you and abandon my wild efforts to restore the Lawrence Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Interesting, now you want to talk. Seems you've had a change of heart.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: In that case, maybe you'll be able to explain everything in detail for us now?

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: I, uh... I admit it. Yes, I came here in hopes of finding a way to restore the Lawrence Clan to its former glory.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: But it was a long journey, and I didn't always know the way. I passed through Liyue and Sumeru... and there was even a time when I lost my wallet and had to live in the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: But the peculiar thing is... I realized that nobody knew me out there, and not a single person even cared about the Lawrence Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: You and I are like glass pawns that were raised in shackles. We were taught to act like nobles, but outside the walls of our home, the people of Mondstadt despised us.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Such pompous, hateful, and stubborn teaching... It all culminated to making us cling to the old aristocratic dogma in an attempt to maintain our pride.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: It's like a never-ending game of tug-of-war. But it is meaningless... You understand. Or I should say, you have already long understood, but I'm afraid that I have only just realized this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon sorta understands what Lessig is saying.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Everything he said is true. Your family is probably unaware that you've already changed how you see things.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Yes, this has all happened recently. After coming to this domain, I realized the Mondstadt that I want is one where not everyone fears me.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: All that I and many other members of the Lawrence Clan long for is a place where we can live peacefully with others.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Lessig, both you and I never had anything to do with the glory of the Lawrence Clan. That is all in the past, we are just ordinary people.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: I originally planned on returning to Mondstadt after taking care of things here. I never thought you would come here. I was completely shocked, which is why I reacted like I did. I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: See, people can always make different choices, and it seems that Lessig has also chosen to become someone he truly wants to be.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Ah yes, about that... I'm afraid I haven't quite found my own purpose in life yet...

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: That's alright. Being able to clearly choose between becoming who you want to be and who your parents wanted you to be is already a step in the right direction.

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: How to find true happiness is probably one of the most difficult research topics of all.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: I have a suggestion for you, Lessig.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Why don't you return to Mondstadt and tell your parents what you just told us?

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Hah, they'll probably try to tear me limb from limb. But what about you? Did you ever tell your family about what you think?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: This is something that I've been thinking about, too. Perhaps the two of us can sit down with the rest of the clan and discuss it with them.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: The Lawrence Clan is just like this stage. It was once home to glorious performances, but those days are now long gone, and it is time for the stage to be updated.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (She's so solid and tough, but also clear and open... like an ice cube. Is that why she's able to dance anytime and anywhere she wishes?)

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Uh, are you all done talking now?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Yes, I think so. By the way, that is for you, please take it. I found it on Lessig earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Oh! It's one of the missing components! Wait, so you had it all this time? Why didn't you give it to me earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Maymunah
dialogues.text: Well, you didn't ask! Alright, I admit it... I forgot about it.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: #Hehe... Okay, we'll let {NICKNAME} hold on to it for now.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Hmm? Wait, this looks like...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks pretty familiar... Have we seen one of these before?

choices.text: Many times... Some might say too many...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shh! Now's not the time to brag about being a hero!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Ah right, I also bought a similar box at the last festival.

response.speaker: Maymunah
response.text: Yes, people often use this kind of box for candy at festivals. This was one of the "materials" originally used to create the tent.

response.speaker: Maymunah
response.text: But now that the tent has been repaired, we no longer need it.

response.speaker: Maymunah
response.text: Eating the candy from the box as an adult will never be as delicious as it was when you were a kid. But if you really think about it, there are way more things you can eat as an adult.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! So when it comes down to it, eating candy is sorta like life, it's just another choice!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: So as of now, we've already collected three of the missing components. Only one more to go!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I'm sorry that repairing the tent took so much of everyone's time. You should all head back and have a rest, I'll lead the way...

talks.objective: Return to the Silver Bottle Courtyard

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Kokomi! You're already here.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back. I trust your adventures to the forest went smoothly?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, you could say that! How about you? Up to anything today?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Well, I suppose it's time I told you that as the Divine Priestess of Watatsumi Island, I shouldn't actually be here now.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: The truth is that a relic, known as the Shinrou Casket, was lost from Watatsumi Island long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: But recently, an orb matching the relic's description suddenly began emitting light, almost as if it was guiding people to it. This is what led me to find the relic's whereabouts.

choices.text: So you came here looking for something...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I wasn't lying when I said that. Gorou has often told me that sitting at home reading light novels is not the best of practices, and that I should try to get out more.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: As I made my way from Watatsumi Island to Sumeru, I enjoyed a variety of breathtaking sights. It really is a beautiful nation. I even stayed in the rainforest for several days.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I was surprised to find that the relic had ended up in the desert. I knew it was somewhere here, but I still couldn't pinpoint the exact location.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Though I feel that Idyia was not intentionally trying to hide anything from us, this domain does have plenty of secrets. I'm sure you've sensed that, too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This is an unusual place, and Idyia would suddenly become very busy from time to time. Plus, she knows Alice...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you mention it, a lot did happen today.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Kokomi everything that happened at the fairgrounds...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I see. When you found Lessig, did you also happen to find any clues related to this domain?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No, I don't think so.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I'm afraid that he was caught up in his thoughts and didn't pay attention to his surroundings. Actually, before the "world was flipped upside down," this domain didn't look anything like this.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Hey everyone! Oh, I hope we're not interrupting your conversation...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: It's alright, you two did a lot today. Care to join me for a cup of tea?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Sure, that would be perfect! Eula and I just made some snacks...

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Turns out that Idyia has a cooking stove and oven. Seriously, why didn't she mention it earlier...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So did you make us some Moon Pies?

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: #No, I made something called Stormcrest Pie. You should try one, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: And I made some Pita Pockets! You can try some, Kokomi. It should taste great with tea.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Ah, sorry... I should call you General.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Oh, I would be happy to try some.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way Eula, how's your cousin doing now?

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Oh, him... You would never guess, but he's busy over by the oven now.

choices.text: That's what you meant by "broadening your horizons"...
